# Aññāṇakathā (Kv 2.2)

**ID:** Kv 2.2
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Aññāṇakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Aññāṇakathā* (Kv 2.2) is a debate in the second chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The text examines the contentious proposition that an arahant can possess ignorance or lack of knowledge (*aññāṇa*), one of the celebrated "Five Points" traditionally attributed in Buddhist doxography to Mahādeva and contested among the early Buddhist schools [Skorupski 1991; Yao 2005]. In this debate, the interlocutors utilize the less technical term *aññāṇa* rather than *avijjā* [Skorupski 1991; Dutt 1978]. According to the commentary, traditions such as the Pubbaseliyas argued that an arahant might lack knowledge regarding mundane matters—such as the name or lineage of an unfamiliar person or the identity of a tree—even though they are free from spiritual ignorance (*avijjā*) concerning the Four Noble Truths and dependent origination [Dutt 1978; Buswell and Gimello 1992]. The Theravādin rejoinder rejects this concession, insisting that full arhatship entails the eradication of all latent tendencies (*anusaya*) and ignorance [Dutt 1978; Buswell and Gimello 1992].
